speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew's passing, the National Day Parade and other special events helped us appreciate how far we have come since Independence and how precious and unique is the home we have built.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We re-affirmed the values we hold dear; we celebrated the bonds that bind us; and we pledged to work together to build a better Singapore.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: This solidarity will stand us in good stead as we enter our next half century as a sovereign independent nation and embark on a new chapter of nation-building with the Opening of this Parliament.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We are in a stronger position than our founding generation was and have a deeper sense of nationhood.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: But whether it is the next five or 50 years, we cannot expect an easy journey.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The fundamental realities of our existence will not change.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We remain a small country with no natural resources apart from our people.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We earn a living only because we are useful to the rest of the world.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: And in a world where size and power still matter, Singapore thrives only because it safeguards its interests.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Our region has become more integrated with the establishment of the ASEAN Community.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: If ASEAN remains stable and our neighbours prosper, we, too, will prosper.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: But if ASEAN is fraught with tension or our neighbours stumble, we, too, will suffer.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Terrorism has become a dangerous and persistent threat.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Yesterday's bomb blasts in Jakarta are a reminder of how close terrorism can strike.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We are fully on guard against this threat, but we cannot rule out the possibility of an attack in Singapore.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Our first 50 years saw us advance rapidly from Third World to First.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: But now that our economy is more mature, we will grow more slowly.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: With limited land and labour and more severe global competition, we must upgrade our economy to sustain growth.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: But upgrading means restructuring, which means our people and businesses will need to adapt and change.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: What will this mean for our healthcare system?

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Page: 15 We are becoming more diverse, not only in terms of race and religion, but also in our interests and perspectives.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Will we remain a cohesive society, or will our differences pull us apart?

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: How do we ensure our island-nation remains a shining red dot, so that our children and grandchildren will thrive?

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: To remain special, we must first resolve to move ahead together.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We must have a shared understanding of what unites and binds us to one another.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: That is why in the last term, the Government held "Our Singapore Conversation", so that Singaporeans could share their hopes and aspirations with one another.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: That is also why we paid tribute to our Pioneers through the Pioneer Generation Package.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: It was because of our Pioneers' determination to build a multiracial society, their ruggedness and their willingness to sacrifice that we, their children, enjoy better lives.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The tribute to the Pioneer Generation reminded us of our founding values and set the tone for SG50.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Our programmes in the last term of Government reflected our commitment to move forward together.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We strove to leave no one behind, even as we created opportunities for all.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We dealt with pressing concerns in housing, healthcare, transport and population.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The Government also made major shifts in social policy.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Building on policies since 2006, the community and the state took on greater responsibility for individuals and families who needed more support.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: With MediShield Life, all Singaporeans now have lifelong healthcare coverage and peace of mind.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Silver Support will provide support for our seniors in need.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We are connecting our waterways and parks and setting aside green spaces like Pulau Ubin and the Rail Corridor.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Our programmes improved the well-being of all Singaporeans and brought people closer together and will continue to do so.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The people affirmed this by returning the PAP Government to office with a stronger mandate.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: But the work of securing this nation and improving our lives is never-ending.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We must continually adjust our programmes and politics to ensure that Singapore keeps on an upward path.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: In this term of Government, we have five key aims to fulfil: First, we will keep Singapore safe and secure; Second, we will renew our economy; Third, we will foster a more caring society; Fourth, we will transform our urban landscape; and Page: 16 Fifth, we will engage and partner Singaporeans in nation-building.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: First and foremost, we can remain sovereign only if we are able to determine our own fate.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Our geopolitical realities remain unchanged from 50 years ago.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We must continue to invest in our security and expand our international space through diplomacy.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We must resist the impulse to divert attention and resources from security as domestic needs burgeon.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: If we cannot safeguard our sovereignty, we cannot secure our livelihoods.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Attacks elsewhere have shown that terrorism can arise at home and not just come from abroad.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: A terrorist attack here will not only cause death and injury, but could also tear apart our social fabric.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Hence, we must keep our society united and resilient.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Every Singaporean has a role to play in keeping our country safe and preserving our multiracial harmony.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: All must reject violence and keep working to deepen mutual understanding and expand our common spaces.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: If we trust and accept one another "regardless of race, language or religion", we will remain strong and united even if others seek to sow fear and division amongst us.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Second, we must renew our economy so that Singapore will always be a place where our children can chase rainbows and fulfil aspirations.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: There will be winners and losers among companies, with some painful dislocation, but economic progress will, ultimately, benefit all Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We cannot predict the future, but we must adapt as the world changes.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Therefore, we will continue to invest in education, from pre-school to lifelong, so that our people will always have pathways upwards.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We want to build a society where every individual, whatever his background, can do well if he applies himself.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: SkillsFuture can succeed only if it is a movement encompassing workers, companies and Government, parents and students.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Third, we will press on with fostering a caring society that is sustainable over the long term.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We do not want to end up like many developed countries that cannot afford their over-generous welfare schemes.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We will strengthen the primary care sector, so that Singaporeans benefit from long-term partnerships with regular family doctors.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We will build on our regional health systems and partner private sector and VWO healthcare providers to take care services beyond hospital walls.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: But it is not enough and not sustainable to just keep funding more treatment and building more capacity.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: All of us can play our part by living healthily and living well.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: They are valued members of our families, communities and workplaces.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Ours should be a society where the bonds of kinship run deep and people look out for one another, a society where we extend our concern for immediate families and friends to the broader community.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: A society consisting of generous hearts who treat one another with warmth and dignity – including those who have just joined us, or those who are here only a while.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Building a caring society starts with each one of us.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: As a compact city, we can be "car-lite".

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Walking, cycling and riding public transport must become the default for more commuters.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Then, we can all have a higher quality of life.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Our major infrastructure plans will take several terms of Government to complete.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: These are acts of faith in Singapore's future that will benefit our children and Singaporeans yet unborn.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Others will enliven our heartlands and everyday living spaces.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: As we saw in the Future of Us Exhibition, technology can open up many possibilities: for example, with autonomous vehicles, we can build a much more efficient transport network and rely less on private cars.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Ours may be a compact city, but it can be highly liveable, green, energy-efficient and conveniently connected-up.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We can be a "citizen-driven" smart nation, constantly improving through the ideas of people.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We must foster partnership and collaboration amongst citizens so that everyone plays a part in building our nation.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: During SG50, we saw how willing Singaporeans were to contribute and share a part of their lives with one another.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Let us all participate in shaping our common future.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: In doing so, we will strengthen our bonds and deepen trust with one another.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: This was the spirit of Our Singapore Conversation.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Individual aspirations may differ, but we all realised that we must work together to create our common future.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: This spirit was sustained through our SG50 celebrations and profoundly deepened when we mourned the passing of our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The SGfuture dialogues and the Committee on the Future Economy are but two national platforms for us to make our future together.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: I have outlined the Government's programmes for the road ahead.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We have a full agenda and much to do together.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: There are dreams and aspirations to be realised and challenges to be overcomed.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: For our programmes to succeed, we need good politics.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Good policies ensure that all citizens benefit from Singapore's success, fostering a society that encourages everyone to come together in building a nation.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Good politics ensures that we elect governments that develop and deliver on sound policies, strengthen the country and bring people together.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: This was how, for 50 years, we conceived and implemented sound policies to improve the lives of the people.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We had good politics because our policies benefited everyone; and we had good policies because our politics expanded our common spaces.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: How do we ensure our politics continues to work for the long-term good of Singapore?

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Every generation of leaders must develop the next generation consciously and systematically.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Every successive Government must take leadership renewal seriously.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: And every new generation of leaders must win anew the people's trust, for the right to leadership is not transferable from one generation to the next.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We must always hold political leaders to high standards of ability and integrity.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Our system must make it an imperative for every politician to be honest and trusted and to do the right thing for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: We often see countries suffering from deep divisions in their societies and crippled by political gridlock.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: At the same time, our political system must also incorporate appropriate stabilisers and checks and balances.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: It must give opportunities for alternative views to be considered and taken into account.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: It must assure the minority communities that they will not be shut out or marginalised, but can participate fully in the mainstream of national life.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The office of the President is another critical element that fosters resilience and stability in our political system.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Executive power is vested in the Government, but the President holds a second key, with specific custodial powers.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: This helps to ensure that major decisions are taken wisely and prudently, especially decisions to spend the reserves and to make important public sector appointments.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Our political system has delivered stability and progress for Singapore.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: But this system must be refreshed from time to time, as our circumstances change.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The Government will study this matter carefully, to see whether and how we should improve our political system so that we can be assured of clean, effective and accountable government over the long term.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Singaporeans have given the new Government a strong mandate.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: They have sent a clear signal that they want to work with it to build a better and brighter future.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The Government will work closely with the people for the long-term interest of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: The Ministers will mobilise support for their programmes and policies.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: In particular, the younger Ministers will build their experience governing Singapore and their rapport with Singaporeans.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Members of Parliament, new or re-elected, from the ruling party or the opposition, all have a responsibility to do their best for our people.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Fifty years ago, in this House, Mr Lee Kuan Yew called upon Members of Parliament to "leave no stone unturned in seeking a just and enduring future for all the people who make up the society".

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Singapore today is the cohesive and progressive society that our Pioneers strove to build.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: It is for us now to write the next chapter together.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Let us renew our pledge to build a better Singapore as one united people, regardless of race, language or religion.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Let us build a Singapore that leaves a stronger mark on the world than its size suggests.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Page: 19 Together, we will progress as an exceptional nation with a thriving economy and a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The President (Dr Tony Tan Keng Yam)
text: Page: 20 ADDENDA TO PRESIDENT'S ADDRESS AT THE OPENING OF THE FIRST SESSION OF THE THIRTEENTH PARLIAMENT ON FRIDAY, 15 JANUARY 2016
